newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain sacks attorney general after courts crisis.
newsitem.headline: Spain sacks attorney general after courts crisis.

text.p: Spain's cabinet of ministers sacked Attorney General Juan Ortiz Urculo on Friday after a prolonged political crisis in the prosecutor's office of the High Court threatened to bog down the judicial system.
"The Cabinet of Ministers has agreed to relieve the state's Attorney General," government spokesman Miguel Angel Rodriguez told a news conference after the weekly cabinet meeting.
He said the ministers would appoint Jesus Cardenal, chief prosecutor for the Basque region's highest court, as the new attorney general next week.

The problems started at the end of 1996 after Ortiz Urculo ordered an inspection of the High Court prosecutor's office and fired the chief prosecutor and put sanctions on four others for "irregularities".

Tension between the state Attorney General's office and the High Court prosecutor's office worsened when Ortiz Urculo's candidate for chief prosecutor was criticised for his alleged political leanings and ultimately rejected by the government.
On Friday, the cabinet also approved the transfer of one of the sanctioned prosecutors, a move that had been delayed by the Justice Ministry, adding to the crisis.
Both allies and opposition parties had criticised the government for the delay, accusing it of interfering with the Attorney General's office, which is supposedly independent.
But most politicians hailed the decision to dismiss the controversial Ortiz Urculo.

"It's a politically intelligent decision that is trying to create a sense of serenity and calm in the justice system," said Josep Sanchez, deputy spokesman for the Catalan coalition, which supports the ruling party in congress.
